items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Alice Mam, whom I never heard of before.

ctx.x: The 15th of May 1936, I recorded with Willie Lewis and George Johnson was also engaged for this date which augmented Willie's orchestra to 11 pieces, band plus two singers, one of which was Adelaide Hall who had been famous in many of the New York Cotton Club revues and Alice Mam, whom I never heard of before.

Billy Burns was the trombonist and I had met him only a short time before Willie started broadcasting to England. Billy was a fellow whose complexion was so clear that he could pass for an Italian. He had played in Europe with Sam Wooding who was known to have brought the first Negro Jazz orchestra to Europe after the war of 1914-1918. Burns had also played with Noble Sissle in Europe and Freddy Johnson the pianist whom I had met when I came to Paris in 1933. Burns told me that he had been offered a trombone…
